### Observed differences

- The early step of the process differs between the windows. In the earlier window, every trace ran A02 → A01 → A07: A02 always led to A01, A01 appeared exactly once per trace at about position 0.2 (roughly a fifth into the trace), and always led to A07. In the later window, A01 appears in none of the 200 traces, while A03 appears exactly once per trace at position 0.2; A02 now always leads to A03, and A03 always leads to A07. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- A01's relational role has moved to A03. Earlier, A01 co-occurred with A02, A07 and A05 in 100% of traces and always ran before them; in the later window A03 does so (A02 before A03, A03 before A07, A03 before A05, each in 100% of traces), while every pair containing A01 shows A01 simply absent. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL005, REL006, REL008, REL010]
- A new optional closing activity appears. A06 was absent from all earlier traces; in the later window it occurs once in about 47 in 100 traces (93 of 200), always at the final position and directly after A05. Earlier, outgoing transitions from A05 were observed in only about 101 of 200 traces (all leading to A08), leaving roughly half the traces in which A05 had no observed successor; in the later window A05 always has a successor, leading to A06 in about 47 in 100 cases and to A08 in about 53 in 100. [OCC003, POS004, DIR004, REL004, REL007, REL009, REL011, REL012]
- Two existing steps became more rigid in position. A07, earlier at a mean position of about 0.45 (varying between 0.4 and 0.5), is now always at 0.4; A05, earlier at a mean of about 0.9 (from 0.8 up to the last position), is now always at 0.8. [POS003, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 was removed and A03 inserted in its place at the same early point of the process: A02 now hands over to A03 instead of A01, A03 executes once in every trace at the position A01 used to occupy (about 0.2), and A03 hands over to A07, exactly as A01 did. This rests on direct and mutually consistent signs: the participation flip with full support in both windows (200 of 200 traces down to 0, and 0 up to 200 of 200), the directly observed successor change of A02, the match between A03's outgoing edge and A01's former one, and the complete transfer of A01's co-occurrence and ordering relations to A03. Screening produced 24 qualifying control-flow items where about 0.12 would be expected without any change, so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole, and every item's difference exceeds those seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits. The main limitation is that a relabelling of the same activity (A01 renamed to A03) would leave an identical behavioural footprint, so the evidence cannot separate a true substitution from a rename. [OCC001, OCC002, POS002, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL006]

Other differences: the introduction of A06 as an optional final step after A05 in about 47 in 100 traces, together with A05 now always having a successor where previously about half the traces ended at A05, and the positions of A07 and A05 becoming deterministic; these involve A05, A06 and A08 and are not part of the main hypothesis. Because A06 was not observed at all in the earlier window, the evidence cannot distinguish a newly added step from a previously unobserved path that became frequent. [OCC003, POS004, DIR004, POS003, POS005]
